intro: A strong signal can still lead to a modest posterior when its prior probability is small. Track both the evidence probability and the updated belief.
task: Return a dictionary with posterior probabilities and evidence probability after observing one event under a finite set of hypotheses.
requirements: prior is a probability vector and likelihood has the same shape with values in [0,1]. The sum of prior times likelihood must be positive.
Return {"posterior": prior*likelihood/evidence, "evidence": evidence}, where evidence is the sum of the joint masses.
Preserve hypotheses with zero prior at zero posterior. Do not renormalize the likelihood across hypotheses.

Use real finite numeric inputs with magnitude at most 1e6, excluding booleans. Vectors have length 1..128 and matrix axes have length 1..128 unless a tighter bound is stated. Leave all inputs unchanged; raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

examples.name: Unequal prior
Uninformative event
Impossible hypothesis

hints.title: Find the structure
hints.body: First calculate one joint mass for every hypothesis by combining its prior with the event likelihood.

hints.title: Build the calculation
hints.body: The normalization constant is also the event probability; keep it before dividing the joint masses.

explanation: Bayes updating multiplies a prior by a likelihood before dividing by the total evidence. The evidence is a weighted average of likelihoods, not their unweighted sum.
The event probability also diagnoses impossible observations. Returning both quantities makes it possible to audit where a surprising posterior came from.
